questions.question: Explain how transistor amplifies a weak signal? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how transistor
  • amplifies a weak
  • signal?
  • A weak signal applied to the base-emitter (low resistance) junction causes small
  • variations in base current Δ I B.
  • Due to transistor action,Δ IC=β × Δ I B, producing large collector current variation.
  • This large current change through the high-resistance collector load produces a large
  • output voltage, achieving amplification.

questions.question: Derive the expression for current in an LCR series circuit and discuss its variation with frequency. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Derive the expression
  • for current in an LCR
  • series circuit and
  • discuss its variation
  • with frequency.
  • Applied voltage: V = Vm sin(ωt)
  • Impedance: Z = √[R² + (XL − XC)²]
  • Current: I = V/Z = Vm/Z sin(ωt − φ)
  • Phase angle: tanφ = (XL − XC)/R
  • Frequency variation:
  • At low f: XC > XL, circuit is capacitive, I lags V.
  • At resonance f0 = 1/(2π√LC): XL = XC, Z = R (minimum), I is maximum.
  • At high f: XL > XC, circuit is inductive, I leads V.

questions.question: Explain the mechanism by which a Zener diode keeps the output voltage constant when the input supply voltage varies. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the mechanism
  • by which a Zener diode
  • keeps the output
  • voltage constant when
  • the input supply voltage
  • varies.
  • The Zener diode is connected in reverse bias with a series resistor Rs.
  • When input voltage Vin increases: extra current flows through Rs; excess current is
  • diverted through Zener, so Vout remains constant at VZ.
  • When Vin decreases: Zener current decreases, less voltage drops across Rs, Vout stays
  • at VZ.
  • The Zener operates in the breakdown region where V−I curve is nearly vertical,
  • maintaining constant voltage.
